summary: Prince William County fire tower on Bull Run Mountain, funded 1941, built 1942, removed by 1979 and reported demolished; no source describes the summit today beyond a survey benchmark.

facts.status_note: Removed between 1966 and 1979; a 1979 report said it had been demolished.

access.note: The register lists the site as administered by a private owner; no source we read says visitors are welcome.

events.note: County board authorized up to $350 for a tower at the request of district forester Berlin Eye; the Evening Star reported the appropriation on September 15
Built year on the register record
Located by the USGS; used as a landmark for the Jackson Hollow benchmark
Removal dated between 1966 and 1979; a 1979 report said the tower had been demolished
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the authorization to September 4, 1941; the Evening Star report of September 15 gives the same $350 figure. The dates differ because one records the board decision and the other a later newspaper report, so this is not a real disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. The register's built year (1942) rests on its Built field, and the quote is the bare year. The register's removal is a span (between 1966 and 1979), with a 1979 demolition report. The Forest Lookouts page gives only the word Removed plus the 1941 newspaper item and a 1954 survey description. No source describes what remains at the summit today. The benchmark description is quoted as published and its date is not stated beyond the 1954 stamp. Access is inferred from the register's private-owner entry, not from any visitor policy.
